bibliography.note: authors, year, title, journal, 62(8): 1720–1732 match Crossref. The text read is the interim report; a reader with access to the CJFAS version could confirm that Tables 3–4 and the diet paragraph are unchanged in print

claims.claim: at 5–10 cm, plankton 72 % and insects 28 % of the diet (four fish); fish from 10–15 cm (Opeongo)
claims.location: p. 31 (PDF p. 33), Table 4 (read on the page image and in the raw text)
claims.conditions: Lake Opeongo, summer 2002; 'mean percent occurrence of prey items' (not mass or volume); Op 5–10 cm N = 4 (0 % empty); Op 10–15 cm: fish 43 % (SE 18), N = 9; fish 0 % in both lakes' 5–10-cm class
claims.note: the Provoking 5–10-cm fish (N = 5) differed: plankton 25 %, insects 12 %, 'other' 62 %

claims.paper: Table 3.7-2 (Lake Opeongo / Provoking Lake row), empty stomachs
claims.claim: adult smallmouth bass: 35 % (Opeongo) and 40 % (Provoking) empty stomachs
claims.quote: For adults, the percent of empty stomachs was 40% for Provoking and 35%
claims.conditions: summer 2002 samples (trap nets, minnow traps, angling; frozen fish); all sizes: 33 % Provoking, 29 % Opeongo empty

claims.paper: Table 3.7-2 (Lake Opeongo / Provoking Lake row), column 'Contents of fed stomachs'
claims.claim: 4.3 g / 1.9 g per stomach (Opeongo / Provoking), adults, fed stomachs
claims.source_value: mean stomach-content mass 4.3 g (SE 1.2, N = 43) at Opeongo and 1.9 g (SE 1.0, N = 25) at Provoking, summer 2002; the source does not say these are adults or fed stomachs only
claims.conditions: summer 2002; masses ln-transformed for the ANOVA (F1,87 = 10.3); the sample behind the means is not defined
claims.note: the digits are right but the row's labels 'adults' and 'fed stomachs' are the paper's. The Ns argue against 'adults': Opeongo's N = 43 is close to all its fed fish of every size (62 fish, 29 % empty ≈ 44 fed; Table 3), not its fed adults (35 fish ≥ 20 cm in Table 4, 35 % empty ≈ 23). Give the masses as 'mean stomach contents, summer 2002 (N = 43 / 25)'

claims.claim: crayfish made up 71 % of the diet of Opeongo bass over 25 cm
claims.location: p. 19 (PDF p. 21), Results: Diet; p. 31 (PDF p. 33), Table 4
claims.quote: percentage of crayfish in the diet increased until it made up 71% of the diet
claims.conditions: Lake Opeongo, summer 2002, bass > 25 cm, N = 19 (SE 11); mean percent occurrence of prey items
claims.note: the sentence sets it beside Tester's 72–79 % of food volume; Dunlop's measure is percent occurrence, not volume

claims.claim: where crayfish are scarce bass turn to insects rather than fish: insects 61–72 % of stomach contents (juveniles and adults pooled) in Provoking Lake, where growth fell behind at the size at which Opeongo bass switch to crayfish
claims.location: p. 30 (PDF p. 32), Table 3; p. 20 (PDF p. 22), Results: Diet
claims.quote: Provoking started to fall behind Opeongo at the size (15-20 cm) when crayfish first appeared
claims.conditions: Table 3, pooled juveniles and adults, mean percent occurrence: Provoking insects 61 % (1981, N = 138), 72 % (1982, N = 64), 62 % (2002, N = 60); crayfish 2–14 %, fish 3–16 % (fish not different from Opeongo's 14–16 %)

claims.claim: young smallmouth in Lake Opeongo first took fish at 10–15 cm
claims.conditions: Opeongo, summer 2002: fish 0 % at 5–10 cm (N = 4), 43 % at 10–15 cm (N = 9); the Discussion (p. 22) puts the first fish at 10–20 cm

claims.location: p. 30 (PDF p. 32), Table 3 (% Empty column); pp. 18–19 (PDF pp. 20–21)
claims.conditions: pooled juveniles and adults: Provoking 50 % (1981), 30 % (1982), 33 % (2002); Opeongo 23 % (1981), 29 % (2002); Bridle 13 % (1982); adults 2002: 35–40 %; by size class (Table 4) 0–50 %
claims.note: a loose summary: most values lie in 25–50 %, but Opeongo 1981 (23 %) and low-density Bridle (13 %) fall below it

claims.claim: young smallmouth eat plankton and insects to ~10 cm, fish appearing at 10–15 cm
claims.location: p. 19 (PDF p. 21), Results: Diet; p. 31 (PDF p. 33), Table 4
claims.quote: diet of 5-10 cm bass in both populations consisted of small-bodied prey
claims.conditions: body-length classes, summer 2002, small samples (N = 4–9 per class at Opeongo)
claims.note: the source gives length classes, not ages: it does not say its 5–10-cm summer fish are young of the year, as the code's 'the year's young' implies

notes: Other useful values in the source: Provoking 3,741 vs Opeongo 82 adults/km² (Orendorff 1983); littoral (1–1.5 m) days above 15 °C 122 vs 111 and above 20 °C 66 vs 56 (2001); length at 50 % maturity Provoking 22 cm males / 21 cm females, Opeongo 24 / 26 cm (Table 2, fork length); first-time nesting male non-return ('mortality') 0.46–1.0 by age (Table 5); 24-h egg loss after male removal higher at Opeongo (Fig. 6); somatic energy density falls with size at Provoking from ~12–17 cm. Transplanted Provoking bass were 14 % empty against 30 % for residents (1982).
